# chapter: # Sources and fetch notes live in resources/sources/07/SOURCES.md. House = CHRG-117hhrg45085; Senate = S. Hrg. 117-429 / CHRG-117shrg46569.

claim as made in prose: Blount testified that Colonial believed the attacker exploited a legacy VPN profile not intended to be in use
source: Senate hearing, Blount oral statement, transcript lines 364–376 (senate-hearing-2021-06-08.txt)

claim as made in prose: Blount said Colonial could not see the legacy VPN and it did not show up in penetration testing; the public record does not explain why
source: Senate hearing, Hassan/Blount, transcript lines 1118–1140 (senate-hearing-2021-06-08.txt)

claim as made in prose: DOJ put the approximately 75-bitcoin payment on 8 May; Peters said Blount had affirmed a $4.4 million ransom payment, and Blount described choosing to pay
source: DOJ press release 2021-06-07 (doj-seizure-2021-06-07.txt); Senate hearing, Peters/Blount, transcript lines 534–546 and PDF text lines 514–526 (senate-hearing-2021-06-08.txt)

claim as made in prose: Colonial found a ransom note in its IT network just before 5 a.m. on 7 May; an operations supervisor ordered the shutdown, begun about 5:55 and complete across 5,500 miles by 6:10
source: Blount prepared statement §§II, IV, Senate Appendix pp. 42–46 (blount-senate-testimony.txt)

claim as made in prose: Colonial began returning its pipelines to service on Wednesday evening, 12 May
source: Blount prepared statement §IV, Senate Appendix pp. 42–46 (blount-senate-testimony.txt)

claim as made in prose: Blount said Colonial was ready to share the results of its Mandiant-supported review with the Senate committee and that similar legacy assets were not unusual; no public results are in the gathered record
source: Senate hearing, Ossoff/Blount, transcript lines 1692–1702 and PDF text lines 1615–1627; source inventory in SOURCES.md (senate-hearing-2021-06-08.txt)

claim as made in prose: Blount said the particular legacy VPN used single-factor authentication and a complicated password, while Colonial's normal remote access used an RSA token
source: Senate hearing, Portman/Blount, transcript lines 674–700 (senate-hearing-2021-06-08.txt)

claim as made in prose: Blount's statement said the credential source was still under investigation, the legacy profile was shut down, additional protections were implemented, and Dragos and Black Hills specialists were engaged
source: Blount prepared statement §V, Senate Appendix pp. 42–46 (blount-senate-testimony.txt; also House transcript lines 984–998)

claim as made in prose: Colonial had not yet taken up TSA's offered VADR review; Blount said it was scheduled for late July and probably would not have found the legacy VPN because it was questionnaire-based
source: Senate hearing, Hawley/Blount, PDF text lines 1423–1454 and transcript lines 1508–1520 (senate-hearing-2021-06-08.txt)

claim as made in prose: Blount said Colonial shut down to contain the attack and protect OT because it did not yet know the attack's origin or scope
source: Blount prepared statement §§II, IV, Senate Appendix pp. 42–46 (blount-senate-testimony.txt)

claim as made in prose: Mandiant had not previously advised Colonial and was engaged by Hunton Andrews Kurth on Colonial's behalf early on 7 May 2021
source: House hearing, Carmakal prepared statement, transcript lines 1192–1215 (house-hearing-2021-06-09.txt)

claim as made in prose: Mandiant's earliest evidence was an April 29 login to a VPN appliance with a legacy profile, employee username and password; the profile required no one-time passcode
source: House hearing, Carmakal prepared statement, transcript lines 1192–1215 (house-hearing-2021-06-09.txt)

claim as made in prose: Carmakal called the condition a misconfiguration: a legacy VPN profile believed inactive accepted an employee username and password; he said the credential's acquisition route was uncertain
source: House hearing, Thompson/Carmakal, transcript lines 1420–1452 (house-hearing-2021-06-09.txt)

claim as made in prose: Carmakal said one person had legitimate password access as far as Mandiant knew, and that the password had been stolen from another website although its exact source was unknown
source: House hearing, Jackson Lee/Carmakal, transcript lines 1668–1712 (house-hearing-2021-06-09.txt)

claim as made in prose: Carmakal said the legacy profile was completely removed and Colonial VPN logins then required a password plus one-time code
source: House hearing, Thompson/Carmakal, transcript lines 1420–1452 (house-hearing-2021-06-09.txt)

claim as made in prose: CISA/FBI said DarkSide hit Colonial's IT network with no indication at that time of direct OT impact, described the affiliate-based RaaS model, and recommended MFA for remote IT and OT access
source: CISA/FBI Joint Advisory AA21-131A, Summary, Technical Details, Mitigations (cisa-aa21-131a.txt)

claim as made in prose: CNN carried Bloomberg's disused-VPN, no-MFA and dark-web-batch account and attributed to Carmakal that there was no employee phishing evidence or earlier activity before April 29
source: CNN, Fung and Sands, 2021-06-04, quoted passages (cnn-2021-06-04.txt); Bloomberg direct opening incomplete (bloomberg-2021-06-04.txt)

claim as made in prose: The 2019 study covered over 350,000 hijacking attempts; Table 3 reports security-key prevention at 100% ±25% for bots and 100% ±28% for phishing with no targeted figure; Table 7 reports 88.2% same-session success for two-factor users and 89.5% for password-only users
source: Doerfler et al., WWW 2019, abstract, Table 3, §5.3 and Table 7 (doerfler-2019-login-challenges.txt)

claim as made in prose: DOJ announced seizure of 63.7 bitcoins then valued around $2.3 million from an address for which the FBI had the private key; its release does not explain how the key was obtained
source: DOJ press release 2021-06-07 (doj-seizure-2021-06-07.txt); source-availability note in SOURCES.md

claim as made in prose: The FBI attributed the Colonial Pipeline network compromise to DarkSide ransomware on 10 May 2021
source: FBI statement 2021-05-10 (fbi-statement-2021-05-10.txt)

claim as made in prose: The Federal Register records SD-01 issued 26 May 2021 with reporting, coordinator and self-assessment duties, and SD-02 issued 19 July with mitigations, a contingency plan and annual third-party architecture review
GAO said TSA used voluntary pipeline-security guidelines and reviews before May 2021 and had addressed 12 of 15 recommendations from its 2018–19 reports
Google reported zero exclusive security-key users phished in its investigation, 90% prevention for device prompts, 76% for SMS against targeted attacks, and 38% without their phone when challenged
source: Google Security Blog, Thomas and Moscicki, 2019-05-17 (google-2019-account-hygiene.txt)

claim as made in prose: Senator Hassan summarized the testimony as no two-step authentication and called the VPN old before Blount clarified the legacy profile was unseen in penetration tests
source: Senate hearing, Hassan/Blount, transcript lines 1118–1140 (senate-hearing-2021-06-08.txt)

claim as made in prose: Krebs reported Google's 85,000-plus staff claim; Google's spokesperson instead said there had been no reported or confirmed account takeovers since security keys were implemented
source: Krebs on Security, 2018-07-23 (krebs-2018-security-keys.txt)

claim as made in prose: Google's 2016 paper says OTP second factors remain vulnerable to phishing, describes a two-year deployment beginning inside Google, and says a security key tests user presence while signing the server challenge through the requesting browser
source: Lang et al., FC 2016, abstract, §1, §§4.1–4.2 (lang-2016-security-keys.txt)

claim as made in prose: Senator Peters opened the 8 June hearing by attributing the compromised-VPN-password account to recent news reports
source: Senate hearing, Peters opening, transcript lines 228–246 (senate-hearing-2021-06-08.txt)

claim as made in prose: The public 2024 SD-02E says it continues measures first issued in July 2021 and requires MFA or controls providing commensurate mitigation, with a control-room exception requiring compensating controls
source: TSA SD Pipeline-2021-02E (2024), purpose and §III.C.2 (tsa-sd-pipeline-2021-02e.txt)

claim as made in prose: Uber said a contractor initially rejected repeated two-factor prompts but eventually accepted one, allowing an attacker with the contractor's password to log in
source: Uber, “Security update,” 2022-09-16/19 (uber-2022-security-update.txt)

claim as made in prose: WebAuthn scopes public-key credentials to origins belonging to the relying party, enforced jointly by user agents and authenticators
source: W3C Web Authentication Level 3 §1 (webauthn-l3.txt)

claim as made in prose: Wikipedia describes an inactive VPN account without MFA and says the attack afflicted computerized equipment managing the pipeline
source: Wikipedia, “Colonial Pipeline ransomware attack,” saved excerpt 2026-09-02 (wikipedia-colonial.txt)
